title: My Claude Code-developed Diablo clone
author: Pristine-Tonight-411
selftext:
I was bored and since I had a Claude Pro subscription anyway I thought I'll ask it to whip up a Diablo clone for fun. Two weeks later (because Pro is so limited) here's what it cooked up:

**Barrowlight** is a browser-based, 100% AI generated 2.5D pixel-art clone of games like Diablo or PoE. It can be played solo (no internet connection needed after initial loading) or online with 1-4 players on a dedicated server. 

Current features:

\- Three distinct classes (Warrior, Paladin and Sorcerer) with 10 skills each.  
\- Talent trees for each classes  
\- Level cap is currently 35 with a Paragon system extending it to infinity.  
\- 16 dungeon levels, randomly generated (actually just 15 of them are, level 16 is the final boss room) in three biomes, each with their own distinctive looks and monsters  
\- three difficulty levels (normal/nightmare/hell) which require defeating the previous difficulty's final boss to unlock  
\- end game "rifts", randomly generated, with affixes that make them harder and/or more lucrative  
\- unique, legendary, and set items   
\- end-game system: the ferryman can be paid with Oboli (which only drop in the end game) in exchange for a guaranteed unique or set item  
\- common and rare items can be upgraded at a cost  
\- most items can be rerolled at an ever increasing cost as well  
\- socketable gems and runes as well as runewords  
\- personal and account-wide stash  
\- achievements, unlockable titles, collections and pets (which collect gold for you)  
\- live-ops events that increase gold/item/oboli drop rate/XP (online play only)  
\- online accounts can be linked to your Discord account for cloud saving. You can also play online as guest and link later if you want.   
\- fully localized in English/German/Spanish/French/Portugese  
\- "voice acting" in English and German only (air quotes because voices have been generated using Piper TTS, which sounds ... interesting)  
\- general asset license is CC0 or public domain, so all visuals/audio are generated in-code only, except for the title screen and logo, which was generated by ChatGPT. That's also the reason the game looks like it does ...

Pretty sure I missed something here, but I didn't want to use AI to write the post as well. I still have stuff in the pipeline (like a second ranged class for example) so I'm not going to stop as long as it's fun.

If you're up for a playtest, you can visit  [https://play.barrowlight.net](https://play.barrowlight.net)  
If you do, it would be preferred if you play online to test the server. Live Events only apply when playing on the Server, and that feature is the latest addition, which still requires playtesting.

A link to the Discord server is available in-game. Feel free to hop in if you'd like a chat or find any bugs or issues.

**But why?**

Because I wanted to see what Claude Code can do. I do have a background in game development as a hobby, but I haven't developed a game in many years because I became uninterested in torturing myself with Unity. I had never used genAI for game development before.  
  
I know the Diablo-like space has been done to death, and there's probably little value in Barrowlight game-play wise. As it's entirely AI generated it's also pretty soulless. But it works well, and plays quite decent, if you ignore the graphics and SFX. It has it's own rustic charm if you are as old as I am.

I also wanted to learn how server-based games work in terms of hosting and management. While Claude developed it all, I did learn a lot about stuff I didn't know much about, like Docker and Cloudflare.

**Workflow**

I initially used Claude Fable (as I had promo credits), had it analyze the Diablo/PoE-style game genre, and write a concept and plan. Once my Fable credits ran out, I switched to Opus 5 to create an MVP. After the game became generally playable, I switched to Sonnet to save quota, which worked quite well. 

Most design decisions were made by Claude, I only suggested some features or made decisions Claude didn't want to make. The game is written in Typescript. Claude has written a full test suite of over 460 tests by now which are all required to pass before making any commits.

Once most of the code was implemented, I had it run a hardening pass for the server code, which revealed a few rather serious issues, and fixed them. Hopefully.

If we're talking about how many tokens have been spent, I sadly have no idea. I only know I used my entire weekly alotment for two weeks.

Interestingly, despite many Claude Code users reporting that Opus and Sonnet make a lot of mistakes, there were no glaring issues during development. I playtested most of the changes myself and while some things needed refinement, there weren't any real bugs. Despite Sonnet being clearly the weakest model (and loved to use subagents for nonsense) it never managed to break anything.
